title: The Sky-Chamber Where Wind Learns to Read

features.name: the reading-wind
features.desc-on-touch: Air that has learned to interpret. It carries messages not by sound, but by knowing how to move through the reader's own stillness.

features.name: the silence-antenna
features.desc-on-touch: A transmission structure that works only when it stops broadcasting. Every quiet moment it sends carries information the noise would have erased.

features.name: the text-that-moves
features.desc-on-touch: Words written on paper so thin the wind can carry them without tearing them. They arrive at their destination still readable, slightly bent.

features.name: the resonance-hollow
features.desc-on-touch: A chamber shaped to amplify only silence. When the wind passes through, it learns new meanings from what is not there.

features.name: the breath-marker
features.desc-on-touch: A place where the wind has learned to mark time by breathing. Each gust is a letter. The alphabet is made of pauses.

inscription: the wind learned to read by becoming quiet; now it carries information the air itself was too loud to carry before

file.name: Silent_Transmission_Log_Archive.mp3
file.note: Field recordings of wind moving through increasingly quiet spaces. As the noise floor drops, new patterns emerge—faint but persistent.
